scorecard.note: Every listed setup is a call, written down before the outcome and scored as a reader could trade it: a buy that waits for a daily close fills at the next session's open, a daily close below the out line sells at the next open, the target when it trades, the time stop at the close of twice the horizon, at most 40 sessions (a wave call's measured to its second target). A wave call takes a fifth off at its first target and holds the rest for its second. Earlier calls keep the rule they were listed with: filled and sold at that close.

move.method: VIX close / 15.87: about 81% of days stay inside this move (not 68%). The 68% band is the HAR forecast of the S&P's volatility x 0.88.

fear.method: Fear day = the Buy List's rule: SPY fell 1% or more on the day, or closed under its 50-day average (or a volatility spike). Stress is a separate word from the VIX (under 15 calm, 15 to 18.5 normal, over 18.5 stressed) beside a HAR forecast of the S&P's realized volatility.

tape.delay: the session's prints to the run; the side is signed against the latest quote
labels: side: signed against the latest quote (the options feed has no quote history); mid and unknown prints stay neutral
heat baselines: point-in-time expanding means over the contract's own earlier prints that day; avg_oi is the chain mean
algo ratio tallies are scaled x10 (the desk's choice); the buys-only variant is the vendor's intake, both are shown
multi-leg prints count in the totals and not in the net premium; cancelled prints are excluded entirely
opening or closing: asserted only where the day's numbers force it (volume above open interest; a bid-side print offset by earlier ask-side volume); otherwise unclear
